title: Inertia
theory:
**Big idea:** Bodies "resist" changes to their motion. This resistance is called **inertia**, and **mass** is its measure.

**Two ways to say it**
1. **Loosely:** a body does not change its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a straight line, unless a force makes it. This unwillingness to change is **inertia**.
2. **Precisely:** if the **same force** acts on two particles, the one that gets the **smaller acceleration** has more inertia. Since a = F/m, **larger mass means smaller acceleration, which means more inertia**.

**Everyday inertia**
| Situation | What inertia does |
|---|---|
| A bus starts suddenly | Your body tends to stay at rest, so you fall backward |
| A bus brakes suddenly | Your body tends to keep moving, so you lurch forward |
| A cloth is pulled quickly from under a glass | The glass tends to stay at rest |
| Pushing an empty vs a loaded trolley | The loaded one (more mass) is harder to speed up |

**🧮 Comparison:** the same 20 N force gives a 2 kg body 10 m/s², but a 10 kg body only 2 m/s². The 10 kg body has **5 times the inertia**.

> ⚠️ **Common misconception:** "Inertia is a force that keeps things moving." Inertia is a **property** of matter, measured by mass. It is not a force.

questions.prompt: Inertia is the property of a body by which it:

options.text: Resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion

questions.explanation: Inertia is the unwillingness to change the state of rest or uniform straight-line motion.

questions.prompt: The measure of the inertia of a body is its:
questions.explanation: Larger mass means smaller acceleration for the same force, so mass measures inertia.

questions.prompt: When a bus suddenly brakes, standing passengers lurch forward because:

options.text: Their bodies tend to keep moving forward (inertia)
A pseudo force from the road pushes them

questions.explanation: The bus slows down, but the passengers' bodies tend to continue at the old speed.

questions.prompt: The same force acts on a 2 kg body and a 10 kg body. The ratio of the inertia of the 10 kg body to that of the 2 kg body is:
Which statement about inertia is correct?

options.text: Inertia is a kind of force
A body with more mass gets less acceleration from the same force
Inertia exists only in non-inertial frames

questions.explanation: a = F/m, so more mass means less acceleration. Inertia is a property, not a force.
